newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL STOCKS SEEN RISING, PRESSURE AT 760-770.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL STOCKS SEEN RISING, PRESSURE AT 760-770.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to climb on Monday on the back of institutional and offshore fund buying of large manufacturing stocks, absorbing some of the selling pressure between 760 and 770 points, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed Saturday up 8.83 points to 760.84.
"Institutional investors, taking a positive view of the economy in the long term, are likely to continue buying large manufacturing stocks," said Kim Dae-hee of LG Securities.
However, brokers doubted individual investors would follow.
"Individuals are still hesitant over the economy's prospects and the market lacks positive factors to lure them," said a Dongwon Securities broker.
Brokers said a gradual rise was forecast for this week in anticipation of an economic turnaround aided by the strengthening yen and falling interest rates.
Any developments involving the troubled Kia Group would be closely monitored, but brokers said investors were expected to be less sensitive to news related to Kia this week.
"Investors are getting tired of false Kia-related rumours in the market," said Kim of LG.
